answer: Create 58 slots (partitions/consumers). Per the backpressure lesson's sizing rule, divide peak by what one worker sustains at a target fraction: 100,000 / (2,500 x 0.7) = 57.1, rounded up to 58. Each worker then runs at about 69% of capacity (100,000 / (58 x 2,500)), leaving headroom to lose one worker and still keep up. Sizing to exactly 100% (40 workers) would fall behind as soon as one drops out.
